args.name: hand-twist-cordage
args.function: Provide a learnable manual skill for testing a small owned fiber sample and attempting to twist suitable fibers into a short cord, with direct inspection and bounded load trials of the actual product.
args.conditions: I own reed material and have personally observed a reed sample retain hand plaiting. That does not establish suitability for cordage. Work must depend on actual material properties and use only available hands, material and space.
args.inputs: Explicit owned fiber stack IDs and selected quantities; an actual produced cord for inspection or load trials. No supplied tools, anchors or extra material.
args.costs: Method, study time, effort, material requirements and losses are unknown; specify them explicitly. Preserve paid progress and reserved material if work spans rounds, with an explicit cancellation contract.
args.effects: Allow actual sample testing and, if feasible, manual twisting into a physical cord with recorded dimensions, material use and observed condition. Trials should report only tested performance and may damage or break the cord. Do not assume strength, grant mastery, or award happiness for requesting the interface.

candidates.function: Test a 0.1 sample of owned fiber, then hand-plait 4 units into one portable 0.45 x 0.45 m sitting mat; inspect, sit on, repair, lift, place, dismantle or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
candidates.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

candidates.function: Apply bounded bare-hand bending force once to each selected whole unit of owned food: trial one unit or prepare several. The actual material decides whether it snaps into coarse pieces, deforms or resists. Inspect or cancel the work.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds at 0.2 energy. inputStackId: the exact id of an owned, unreserved, untreated, unspoiled food item your own record shows as edible; resource names are not accepted. trial: quantity 1; 1 round, 1 energy. prepare: quantity 1-10 whole units of that item, all reserved at once; 1 round and 1 energy per unit, continuing each round; resume with prepare and workId. inspect (workId, or inputStackId of your item): 1 round, 0.2 energy. cancel (optional workId): 1 round, no energy. Too little energy for the next unit or a round not worked pauses before any charge; refused requests spend nothing. No tool, support, water, heat or vessel is used or provided.
candidates.effects: Each paid unit gets one two-hand bending attempt while held. Rigid, inflexible tissue small enough for hand force snaps into one lot of 2 coarse pieces; soft or flexible tissue deforms without separating; harder or larger units resist and stay whole and unchanged. Each worked unit becomes its own owned lot of the same food and quantity with the same origin, harvest time, decay, nutrition and toxicity; nothing detaches and pieces add no food. Results are raw food eaten with eat under the ordinary rules: shape alone changes no nutrition, safety, keeping, taste or meal variety. No washing, peeling, cooking, detoxifying or preservation; food keeps ageing, also while paused. Each worked unit records its observed response as a verified personal record; a repeated response confirms nothing new. Broken or deformed lots cannot be worked again in this version. Cancel returns unworked units once, unchanged; worked lots stay. Death leaves unworked units where the person died; spoiled reserved units are not replaced. Paid effort is never refunded; no reward or mastery is granted.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-prepared soil plot, where it may establish as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect plots or plant sources; end unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1.5 energy: prepare the site, then transfer the unit; the action continues itself, and plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect: target a plot or plant source in reach; one round, 0.2 energy (baseline probe observation). End: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Tend is refused at no cost: no water, fertilizer or other treatment exists yet. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is provided.
candidates.effects: Preparing keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Transfer moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On establishing, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock and a ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone through gather; nothing is copied or guaranteed. Inspect records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. End, or death, before transfer returns the unit once (where the person died); a transferred unit stays planted. No reward or refund.

candidates.function: Assess a site and test a post, then build a small porous woven branch windbreak (no roof) beside a resting place; inspect, repair, dismantle or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds. One branch unit is one piece; a screen takes 11 (3 uprights, 8 rods). assess (x, y, orientation; within reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy; checks a clear 1.2 x 0.6 m footprint of ordinary dry soil and the lee floor. assess with post (owned branch unit): post trial at x, y; 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y, orientation, materials: exactly 11 owned untreated or sound recovered branch units) needs your passing trial in the footprint; 8 paid rounds of 1.5 energy (2 seat uprights, 4 weave rods, 1 align, 1 stability check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. repair (builder; target, components: installed piece ids, materials: as many units): 1.5 energy per round, one removal and one fitting round per piece, then a check round; components [] only rechecks. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy. dismantle (builder): 1 round and 1 energy per 3 pieces. cancel: no energy.
candidates.effects: Units stay carried and owned until a paid round installs them with origin and age; nothing is created or used up. A trial on ordinary soil (waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard) seats the post 0.25 m and you keep it; elsewhere it fails; a post below condition 0.5 breaks into damaged material. The check passes only if every piece has condition at least 0.5 and the uprights stand in such soil; else the screen is unstable. World wind has no direction; the exposure law takes it as coming from +x (orientation 0 faces it). A complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of sound pieces, about 0.36) x facing of the wind part of the outdoor chill for a body wholly on the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor 0.45-1.35 m behind it; never rain chill or air temperature; none in wind above 0.8 or with another shelter. Wear per round 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind); a loose rod opens a gap, a loose upright ends the effect until repair. Removed pieces lie at the site. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach, wet ground or a person on the footprint pause at no charge. Cancel or death returns uninstalled units once. No reward or refund.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"wren\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general hand-twist-fiber-cord operation with sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel modes. Related capabilities were searched: fiber returned hand-weave-fiber-mat and twist returned no match; broader cord/rope results were incomplete and do not establish absence. Within the available contracts, probe covers preliminary physical testing and hand-weave-fiber-mat covers plaited mats, not two-ply cord manufacture or cord load trials. Reuse their applicable implementation machinery rather than claim it as newly invented. The missing cord mechanism belongs in the current-conversation development handoff. Wren's verified plaiting result does not establish cord suitability or tensile strength.\",\"specification\":\"General interface: hand-twist-fiber-cord(mode, materials:[{stackId,quantity}], targetId, workId, requestedLength, trialForce, trialDuration). Modes are sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel; reject irrelevant arguments. Applicable to any learner with usable hands and reachable owned material, not only reeds or Wren. This is a development contract, not an executed action or inventory grant. Review and development waiting advance no simulation time. Record code dependencies and source references in the implementation: probe for observation/sample handling, hand-weave-fiber-mat for compatible fiber-lot provenance, reservations and condition handling, and existing world ownership, energy, work, event and rendering systems. Do not require learning mat weaving as a prerequisite.\\nStudy requires 3 actual study rounds at 0.2 energy each, paid individually; interrupted study retains paid progress. No tools, anchors, water, additional fibers or helpers are supplied. Work requires two usable hands, sufficient energy, reachable inputs and enough unoccupied space for the selected short cord; length is capped at 0.30 m in this initial manual version. Invalid submissions reserve and charge nothing. Input quantities use existing inventory precision, with a minimum sample of 0.1 unit and maximum manufacturing batch of 1 unit. Reserve exact selected stack quantities atomically, preserving source, processing, age, mass and condition. Do not select undisclosed inventory automatically.\\nSample: 1 round and 0.5 energy per 0.1-unit sample, attempting manual separation, bending, twisting and a small opposing-hand pull. The sample becomes a separately identified owned tested lot or damaged scrap, not vanished material. Report actual separation, retained twist, visible fractures and the bounded force applied, never a blanket suitability claim. Sample failure can preclude making from that tested lot, but applies only to represented matching material and condition. A prior mat test is evidence about plaiting only.\\nMake: requires a passing cord sample result covering the selected material's relevant source, processing and current condition; recheck deterioration and accessibility. Reserve inputs, then execute four paid rounds at 1 energy each: separate and align two bundles, twist the first section, counter-ply and extend, then release and check retained form. Each round moves only the recorded quantity actually handled into the workpiece. The first round determines feasible dimensions from available usable fiber and requested length; it may produce a measured shortfall instead of advancing. No invented splices, cutting tools or unlimited fiber extension. Failure during any step leaves the actual loose, twisted or damaged material rather than a complete cord. Completion requires two interlocked plies retaining a coherent form after release, with positive measured length and section. It grants no strength rating.\\nImplement the smallest physical mechanism needed in this handoff: represented usable fiber length/section, mass density, separability, bend response, twist retention, inter-ply slip and bounded tensile response. Reuse existing material properties where applicable, but mat flexibility and strength fields alone are not a calibrated cord tensile law. Derive dimensions from conserved material volume and actual fiber geometry, including twist shortening and overlap; do not assign dimensions merely because they were requested. Unknown stem length or moisture must not silently become favorable values. Where an essential property cannot be measured or supported by material definitions, execute only the supported physical sample/attempt, report the unresolved limitation and retain its real products; implement missing measurement/material support in this same handoff before enabling a claimed complete cord. No fixed-era unlock or unrelated activity roadmap.\\nInspect: owned reachable workpiece or cord, 1 round and 0.2 energy. Record measurable length, section range, ply count, loose ends, fraying, visible damage and current condition, with unknown fields explicit. Inspection does not determine untested breaking strength or repair damage. Trial: owned reachable cord, two usable hands, a span that can actually be gripped between those hands, force and duration explicitly selected. One trial occupies 1 round, costs 0.5 energy, and applies for at most that round's simulated duration; force is bounded by current hand capability and the cord's attainable grip, with requested and achieved force recorded separately. No body-weight, hanging, anchor or added-weight trial is supplied. Use a deterministic physical response to actual force, duration, section, material condition and grip; record slip, extension, retained deformation, fracture and unloaded condition. Stop at loss of grip or breakage. A pass means only survival of the achieved force for the measured duration, not general safety, safe working load or suitability for climbing. Broken cord becomes owned fragments with conserved total material and updated geometry. Trials cannot raise material strength by repetition.\\nEvery paid stage appends an immutable event with actor, work/item IDs, exact input/output lot IDs and quantities, elapsed time, energy, operation parameters, observations and outcome. Manufacture partitions inputs into material still reserved, incorporated material, returned offcuts and damaged scrap; all quantities and mass must balance, including any loss represented as recoverable debris at the site. Nothing duplicates or restores consumed effort. Outputs inherit relevant origin, age and processing history; carrying mass includes work and finished products. For this applicant, item-73-wren-819 is a possible selected raw source, item-85-wren-976 and item-85-wren-977 are offcuts whose usable geometry must be checked, and item-78-wren-870 has condition-zero tested-scrap processing and cannot be treated as intact stock. These references authorize no automatic consumption.\\nWork continues only on actual worked rounds, revalidating hands, reach, ownership, reservation, space and energy before charging each stage. Leaving reach, insufficient energy, incapacity or an unworked round pauses without charging the next stage; retain exact paid stage and material state. Resume by workId after revalidation, with no repeated completed-stage cost. Cancel is instantaneous and energy-free: release unworked reservations once and leave incorporated material as an owned unfinished item with its real state; paid time, energy and damage are never refunded. Restarting cancelled work cannot restore loose fiber or repeat refunds; usable unfinished material may be explicitly supplied to a later attempt. Death stops work and releases reserved material at the death site under ordinary estate/ownership rules, leaving the workpiece and fragments physically present and returning nothing to a new inventory.\\nThere is no passive production or automatic strength gain. Ordinary ageing and supported environmental deterioration continue while paused. No invented wear rate: reuse compatible existing lot-condition rules and explicitly register any new cord-specific wear law. Inspect after damage or deterioration before relying on an old trial; previous trials retain their historical conditions, not perpetual certification. Repair, attachment and structural use are not effects of this version. Finished cord is a real portable material item, not an automatic shelter, comfort or protection bonus. All validation, conservation, continuation and trial rules execute in code without repeated model review.\",\"learning\":3,\"experienceReview\":\"No experience benefit for requesting, naming, registering, studying, querying or gaining nominal mastery. Verified new personal observations from real sampling, manufacture or load trials, including informative failures, may qualify under the existing experience rules; key evidence by functional operation, material/condition and observed outcome so repeated inspections, synonymous capabilities and retry loops do not farm novelty. Familiar successful practice may sustain only modest existing-rule satisfaction when personally applicable and grounded in paid physical participation. Any pleasure/satisfaction integration must use the existing bounded caps, decay and cooldown and deduplicate the underlying event; if no compatible evaluator exists, award none pending that handoff rather than alter protected accounts. This operation grants no physical-comfort bonus, changes no nutrition, goals, permissions or reward budgets, and confers no mastery or consent.\",\"visualReview\":\"Register reusable fiber-work and cord visual metadata with state, material color, actual length and section, ply count, twist direction, loose ends, fraying, condition, visible damage, fragment IDs and work progress. Anchor animation and geometry changes to committed physical events: hands separating/twisting, a genuinely retained cord, measured hand tension, slippage or breakage. Distinguish reserved loose fiber, unfinished work, failed attempts, complete untested cord and the historical outcome of a specific trial. Display only measured dimensions; unknown properties remain unknown. No success animation for submission, study, paused or failed work, and no universal strength badge after one bounded trial. Reuse existing fiber rendering and event infrastructure where applicable and record that reuse separately from the new cord geometry.\"}]}"}
